correctness.rationale: The proof reduces local dual curvature to a fixed positive-slack core. The sharp support paper supplies O(ell)-scale sections, O(ell^2) slack height, positive-slack inner balls, and nearby-row overlap. Conditioning on one endpoint converts the core form to a finite-range variance form, whose nonlocal Poincare scale is ell^(d+2)=epsilon. This gives epsilon-uniform strong concavity. Matching test directions establish the bottom and top Hessian scales, and a standalone periodic Fourier calculation reproduces the predicted conditioning law.

originality.rationale: The inspected PL and gradient-convergence papers establish local curvature and linear convergence but not the epsilon-uniform strong-concavity neighborhood or sharp small-epsilon Hessian condition number. The accessible Part I geometry paper explicitly suggests that its estimates can upgrade PL and algorithmic results but does not state the present theorem. Its bibliography cites an inaccessible 2026 working paper, Geometry and Convergence of Quadratically Regularized Optimal Transport II, which is the main unresolved contemporaneous-overlap risk. No accessible source inspected establishes the claimed result. Originality is only to the best of our knowledge.

value.rationale: The theorem identifies the natural optimization scale induced by the new sharp support geometry: an O(1) local PL/strong-concavity modulus on an O(epsilon^(2/(d+2))) potential neighborhood, together with condition number Theta(epsilon^(-2/(d+2))). This explains that weak-regularization stiffness comes from growing maximal curvature rather than vanishing minimal curvature and yields a concrete local step-size law.
